 SALT LAKE CITY (KUTV) — Two consumer-product recalls involve commercial outdoor light fixtures that can fall and gravel bicycles with front wheels that can loosen during use.
 Lithonia Lighting is recalling about 11,532 RSX luminaires with certain adjustable tilt-arm mountings. The knuckle connecting the arm can fail, allowing the fixture to fall and create a serious impact hazard.
 The company has received 13 reports of broken tilt arms, including four reports of fixtures falling. No injuries have been reported.
 The fixtures were sold through commercial distributors nationwide, including Turtle & Hughes and Consolidated Electrical Distributors, from August 2019 through August 2026 for between $400 and $2,200.
 Consumers should keep people clear of the area directly beneath the fixture and contact Lithonia Lighting to schedule a free professional repair. A qualified installer will replace the adjustable arm assembly.

 Decathlon America is also recalling about 1,150 Van Rysel GRVL AF gravel bicycles . The front lock nut can loosen during use, causing the front wheel to dislodge or become loose and creating a crash hazard.
 No incidents or injuries have been reported.
 The recalled bikes were sold at REI Co-op stores nationwide and on REI.com from March 2025 through August 2026 for between $1,400 and $2,300.
 Riders should stop using the recalled bicycles immediately and take them to the nearest REI Co-op for a free inspection and front-fork repair. Consumers unable to visit an REI location can contact Decathlon Customer Service for help.
